title: Cherry Clafoutis
subtitle: French baked custard pudding with fresh cherries
excerpt: Whole cherries baked inside a thick, custardy batter that puffs and sets in a hot oven. A simple, rustic French pudding from the Limousin, wonderful warm from the dish with cream.

recipe.sourceNotes: Clafoutis (from the Limousin dialect word clafir, to fill) is a baked French dessert from the Limousin region of south-central France, where it is made with the region's famous sour black cherries (cerises noires). The traditional Limousin recipe leaves the cherries unpitted: the stones are said to add a subtle almond flavour to the batter during baking, which is the flavour associated with cherry kernels. Outside the traditional region, most cooks pit the cherries for ease of eating. The batter is a simple, thin custard batter similar to a crepe batter: eggs, flour, sugar, milk, cream, and vanilla. It puffs up in the oven and sinks back on cooling. In Limousin, using any fruit other than cherries produces a flognarde rather than a clafoutis, though the term clafoutis is now widely applied to any fruit version. The dish should be eaten warm.

recipeTools.notes: A buttered baking dish or ceramic gratin dish, approximately 28 cm diameter.

content.text: The batter should be mixed until just combined and then rested for 30 minutes: this allows the flour to hydrate and the batter to settle, giving a smoother, more even result. Do not over-mix or the clafoutis will be tough. Butter the dish well and scatter with sugar before adding the cherries and batter: this creates a slightly caramelised base. The clafoutis is done when it is set and golden on top with a very slight wobble in the centre: it will firm up as it cools.
Whisk the eggs and sugar together until combined. Sift in the flour and whisk again until smooth. Add the milk, cream, and vanilla and whisk to a smooth batter. Rest for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Butter the baking dish generously and scatter with 2 tablespoons of sugar. Arrange the cherries in a single layer in the dish. Pour the batter slowly over the cherries.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden on top and just set in the centre. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm from the dish with cream.
